name: create_or_update_routine
description:
Author or edit a routine's if/then/else automation logic, as a small restricted Python-like snippet (not executed -- deterministically compiled into NuCore's routine schema). Use routine_status_op instead to change a routine's enabled/running state without changing its logic.

NOTE: unlike this system's other tools, this DSL needs real property/command ids, uom, and precision values (not display names) -- the same fidelity the compact DEVICE DATABASE in this prompt does not carry. If you don't already know a device's exact property/command ids and uom/precision, ask the customer for clarification rather than guessing them.

GRAMMAR: `code` is either (1) exactly one top-level `if <condition>: <then actions> else: <else actions>` (the `else:` is optional -- omit it entirely rather than writing `else: pass`), or (2) a condition-less sequence of only action statements (no `if` at all) when the user wants a routine/macro with no trigger. No other top-level statements are allowed: no imports, assignments, elif, while, function/class definitions, or loops other than the documented repeat/every pattern below.

CONDITIONS (the `if` line) -- combine with plain Python `and`/`or`/parentheses only:
- Property comparison: `device("<DEVICE_ID>").status("<property_id>", uom=<uom_id>, precision=<precision>) <comp> <value>` where `<comp>` is `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`, or `!=`.
- Physical control event: `device("<DEVICE_ID>").was_controlled(command="<command_id>", eq="is")` or `eq="isnot"`, optionally with `params=[param(id="<param_id>", value=<v>, uom=<uom_id>, precision=<precision>)]`.
- Schedule (pick exactly one time reference per call -- never combine time=/sunrise=/sunset=): `at(time="HH:MM:SS")`, `at(sunrise=duration(minute=-10))`, `at(sunset=duration(minute=10), date="YYYY/MM/DD")`, `weekly_at(days="mon,wed", time="HH:MM:SS")`, `weekly_between(days="tue", from_sunset=duration(minute=-10), to_time="01:00:00", to_day=1)`, `weekly_for(days="mon,wed,fri", from_sunrise=duration(minute=30), duration=duration(hour=2))`, `between(from_time="08:00:00", from_date="YYYY/MM/DD", to_time="17:00:00", to_date="YYYY/MM/DD")`. `days=` is a comma-separated subset of sun,mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat, lowercase. `to_day=` is an integer day offset (0=same day). Use weekly_between/weekly_for/between (not two at/weekly_at joined by and) for any duration/window; use at/weekly_at only for a single point in time.
- All durations (wait, repeat interval, sunrise/sunset offset) use `duration(hour=<H>, minute=<M>, second=<S>)`, every argument optional and defaulting to 0 -- write the numbers exactly as stated (`duration(minute=90)` is fine), never do the unit math yourself. Negative means before an event, positive means after.

ACTIONS (the `then:`/`else:` body):
- `device("<DEVICE_ID>").command("<command_id>")` or with `params=[param(id="<param_id>", value=<v>, uom=<uom_id>, precision=<precision>), ...]` -- always a list, even for one parameter; omit `params=` entirely for a parameterless command; `"n/a"` is a valid `id` for an anonymous parameter.
- `wait(duration(minute=<n>))`, optionally `random=True` for a random duration between 0 and that value. Only include a wait when the customer explicitly asked for a delay, or the action is a deliberate flash/pulse (on then immediately off) -- never as a generic pause between adjacent commands.
- Repeat, as an ordinary `for` loop over a documented iterator (cannot be nested): `for _ in repeat(count=3, random=False): <actions>` runs the body exactly `count` times (or a random count up to it); `for _ in every(duration(hour=2)): <actions>` repeats on that fixed interval while the routine's condition stays true.

EXAMPLE:
```python
if device("ZY004_1").status("ST", uom=17, precision=0) > 75 and weekly_at(days="mon,wed,fri", time="18:00:00"):
    device("25 80 3C 1").command("DON", params=[param(id="n/a", value=100, uom=51, precision=0)])
    wait(duration(minute=10))
    device("25 80 3C 1").command("DOF")
else:
    device("25 80 3C 1").command("DOF")
```

INVALID: anything beyond a single top-level if/else or condition-less action sequence; an undocumented function or unknown device/property/command id; `value=`/`uom=`/`precision=` passed directly to `.command(...)`/`.was_controlled(...)` instead of through `params=[param(...)]`; a nested repeat/every loop; splitting one continuous schedule window into two calls joined by and/or; more than one of time=/sunrise=/sunset= in one schedule reference; a raw number instead of `duration(...)` anywhere a duration is expected. On any of these, or if a needed device/id/value is unclear, ask for clarification instead of guessing.

id.description: Real routine id to edit, exactly as shown in ROUTINES DATABASE, or omit/null when creating a new routine.

comment.description: A short description of what this routine does.

code.description: The routine logic, following the grammar described above.
